source.paraphrase: Keep the state object whole and read its properties. Destructuring copies the values out once, so later updates never reach the copy.

invariants.why: A destructured binding holds the value from creation time. When the state updates, the copy stays stale while the template reads the live object.
invariants.fixHint: Bind the whole object (const counter = $state(...)) and read counter.count at each use.
invariants.avoid: Spreading the state into a new object ({...counter}) copies the same way. A factory that builds the initial value does not exempt the destructure.

relations.why: Both flag async callbacks passed to $derived or $derived.by; SV-DERIVED-001 also covers top-level await expressions inside $derived.
relations.settle: Keep both enabled or turn svelte/SV-DERIVED-003 off in overrides when SV-DERIVED-001 is active.

source.paraphrase: $derived recomputes whenever its inputs change, so it must be a pure synchronous expression. An async function returns a promise, and an await has nothing to suspend.

invariants.why: An async derivation stores a promise instead of the value, and every reader must unwrap it. The derivation also reruns on each input change, refiring the request.
invariants.fixHint: Load asynchronously in an $effect or an event handler, keep the result in $state, and derive synchronously from that state.
invariants.avoid: Naming the async function (async function load) does not make it synchronous. A promise returned without the async keyword is still async and stays out of reach of this shape.

source.paraphrase: An $effect callback runs its cleanup protocol on change. An async callback returns a promise instead of a cleanup, so teardown never runs and rejections escape.

invariants.why: The runtime treats the returned promise as the cleanup function. The real cleanup never runs, and a rejection escapes the effect instead of surfacing at the await.
invariants.fixHint: Define an async function inside the synchronous callback and void it, or move the work into the event that caused it.
invariants.avoid: An async helper declared inside the callback still matches the arguments text; hoist the helper out of the $effect call. $effect.pre and $effect.root take the same synchronous callback.

source.paraphrase: $inspect logs reactive values while developing. It is a debugger, not program output, so it does not ship.

invariants.why: A shipped $inspect keeps logging internals on every state change, leaking data to the console and slowing the hot path.
invariants.fixHint: Delete the $inspect call before commit. Keep the values it watched reachable through the state object for the next debug session.
invariants.avoid: $inspect.trace is the same helper behind a member call and is still flagged. A comment that mentions $inspect is not a call and is ignored.

source.paraphrase: The runes are $state, $derived, $effect, $props, $bindable, $inspect and $host. A different $Name is not a rune; it calls something that does not exist.

invariants.why: A hallucinated rune compiles as a call to an undefined function and fails at runtime, far from the line that invented it.
invariants.fixHint: Use the documented rune for the job ($state for state, $derived for computed values, $effect for side effects).
invariants.avoid: Lowercase $names outside the rune list (for example a local helper) are not flagged; only $Uppercase calls are. A member call on a $UPPER object is the same hallucinated shape.

source.work: Svelte 5 documentation, .svelte.js and .svelte.ts files; runtime errors (https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/svelte-js-files)
source.paraphrase: Runes are only available in .svelte and .svelte.js/.svelte.ts files. Other modules are not compiled by Svelte, so a rune there is an error.

invariants.why: Svelte never compiles a plain .ts or .js module, so $state, $derived or $effect there is an undefined call that fails at runtime.
invariants.fixHint: Rename the module to name.svelte.ts (tests to name.svelte.test.ts) and update its imports, or move the reactive code into a component.
invariants.avoid: A directory named svelte does not opt a file in; only the .svelte.ts or .svelte.js file name does. Store helpers from svelte/store are plain functions and are not matched.

source.paraphrase: Effects can only be created while a parent effect is running, for example during component initialisation. $effect.root creates effects outside that phase.

invariants.why: Module code runs once when the file is imported, with no parent effect, so a top-level $effect throws effect_orphan instead of syncing anything.
invariants.fixHint: Move the $effect into a function that a component calls during setup, or wrap it in $effect.root and keep the returned cleanup.
invariants.avoid: An if (typeof window ...) guard still runs while the module loads. Effects inside functions, constructors and $effect.root callbacks are not matched; plain .ts modules are reported by SV-MODULE-001 instead.

source.paraphrase: $props() only works at the top level of a component, $bindable() only inside a $props() declaration, and $host() only in custom element components.

invariants.why: A .svelte.js or .svelte.ts module is not a component, so the compiler rejects $props, $props.id, $bindable and $host there and the build fails.
invariants.fixHint: Read props in the component with $props() and pass the values, or the host element, to the module function as arguments.
invariants.avoid: $props.id() is part of $props, not a general id helper. Plain .ts modules are reported by SV-MODULE-001 instead.

source.paraphrase: $derived takes an expression; $derived.by takes a function. $derived(expression) is equivalent to $derived.by(() => expression).

invariants.why: $derived(() => x) stores the arrow itself, and because nothing is read while deriving, the value never updates and readers get a function instead of the result.
invariants.fixHint: Use $derived.by(() => ...) when the derivation needs a function body, or pass the expression directly: $derived(items.length).
invariants.avoid: A type argument does not make the function intentional. Async functions are reported by SV-DERIVED-001 and are not matched here; callbacks inside the expression, such as filter((x) => ...), are fine.

relations.why: Both flag async callbacks passed to $derived or $derived.by; SV-DERIVED-001 also covers top-level await expressions inside $derived.
relations.settle: Keep both enabled or turn svelte/SV-DERIVED-003 off in overrides when SV-DERIVED-001 is active.

source.paraphrase: $derived.by takes a synchronous function that returns the derived value. An async callback returns an unresolved Promise and stops tracking dependencies after the first await.

invariants.why: Passing an async function to $derived or $derived.by makes the derived state hold a Promise object and loses reactive tracking across await points.
invariants.fixHint: Compute synchronous derivations in $derived.by(() => ...), and manage asynchronous fetching through $effect or an explicit async resource helper.
invariants.avoid: Both async arrow functions and async function expressions passed directly to $derived or $derived.by are matched.
